title: Graphics Card Payback: Renting Out vs Serving Models
tools: Python data pipeline · JavaScript calculator page · Vast.ai, OpenRouter, InferenceX and GetDeploying data
blurb: A calculator for how many months a data-center GPU takes to pay for itself, renting by the hour or serving open models, across 16 cards.
long: The question: if you purchase a large server GPU (graphics processing unit), how long does it take to break even? The site contrasts two income streams: renting it out hourly on a marketplace, versus using it to host open-weight models and selling the inference on OpenRouter, a marketplace for language model APIs (application programming interface).

Python scripts scrape Vast.ai rental offers, OpenRouter price & traffic per provider, InferenceX throughput tests, and GetDeploying weekly rental prices, as well as my manually maintained list of new/used purchase prices and their sources. The price of server boards is the price of the 8-card server divided by 8 (and 72 for racks). The serving speeds are the fastest measured throughput per card where the user still gets ≥30 tokens/second. If there is no direct test, I copy the serving speed of a similar model and mark it as an estimate.

Each assumption is a control: electricity price, rack-space cost, cooling overhead, fraction of hours rented, which rental price, marketplace fee, which token price, your fraction of a model’s traffic, peak utilisation, and yearly price decrease. At the defaults on this page (data as of 7 October 2026) the fastest rental payback is 17.1 months (used H100 server board) and the fastest serving payback is 5.3 months (Kimi K3 on AMD MI355X, a GPU) but serving revenue is limited by demand, the cheapest providers will take most of the traffic.
A Node script executes the page’s own calc code against the data bundle, verifying the numbers outside the browser.
highlights: Fastest rental payback 17.1 months at defaults
Fastest serving payback 5.3 months at defaults
Ten adjustable assumptions, from electricity price to yearly price drop
